english.title: In charge of premises knowingly cause / permit / fail to prevent use for unlawful broadcasting
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being in charge of premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..), that were used for unlawful broadcasting,

(A)_[knowingly caused the premises to be so used]_
(B)_[knowingly permitted the premises to be so used]_
(C)_[having reasonable cause to believe that the premises were being so used failed to take such steps as were reasonable in the circumstances of the case to prevent them from being so used]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 37 of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being in charge of premises that were used for unlawful broadcasting
knowingly caused/permitted the premises to be so used OR
having reasonable cause to believe that the premises were being so used
failed to take reasonable steps to prevent them from being so used

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 37(4) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that a person is in charge of premises if he is the owner or occupier of the premises; or he has, or acts or assists in, the management or control of premises.
(ii) Section 37(5) of the Act provides that premises are used for unlawful broadcasting if they are used for making an unlawful broadcast; or for sending signals for the operation or control of apparatus used for the purpose of making an unlawful broadcast from another place.
(iii) Section 37(6) of the Act provides that a broadcast is unlawful if it is made by means of the use of a wireless telegraphy station or wireless telegraphy apparatus in contravention of section 8; or the making of the broadcast contravenes a provision of Part 5 (sections 77 - 95).
(iv) Section 37(7) of the Act provides that premises includes any place, vehicle, ship, aircraft, structure or other object (whether movable or not, and whether on land or not).
(v) Section 105 of the Act makes special provisions for this offence in relation to ships and aircraft.
(vi) Section 106 of the Act applies where a person is convicted of this offence and the use continues after the conviction.
(vii) Section 107 of the Act provides for proceedings and enforcement regarding this offence.
(viii) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022, see paragraph 16(a) of Schedule 8 to the Act; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 35(2)(a) of the Act and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
